title: Court-side crowd calling for Minister Sawmynaden’s resignation
location: Courtyard of Saint-Louis Cathedral opposite the New Court House, Port Louis
participants_original: L’Express describes a crowd massed in the cathedral courtyard and sympathizers gathered in support of Simla Kistnen; it reports no count.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved: qualitative references to a “crowd”/“foule massée” show an assembly but the source gives no count and does not securely establish 50 or more.

start_date.summary: The report dated 13 January says the third hearing and crowd activity occurred “yesterday,” i.e. 12 January 2021.

end_date.summary: The report says sympathizers dispersed calmly after the hearing was postponed on 12 January.

location.summary: The report places a crowd in the Saint-Louis Cathedral courtyard by the Port Louis court.

demands.summary: Bystanders chanted for the minister’s resignation over the alleged fictitious constituency-clerk job.

participants_original.summary: The report uses “crowd” and describes sympathizers, but publishes no number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative crowd wording is insufficient by itself to verify the 50-person threshold.

organizer.summary: Bruneau Laurette is reported present early and others joined; the source does not identify an organizer.

protester_violence.summary: The source does not establish whether the Kistnen sympathizers used violence.

state_response.summary: Police are reported moving a separate small pro-minister group away from the sympathizers; the article does not establish the listed response categories against this crowd.

notes: This was a court-side gathering around a private prosecution concerning a government minister, but the crowd made a public demand for the minister’s resignation over alleged fictitious employment. Do not merge it with the separate pro-minister masked group or with the August 2020 Wakashio march. A distinct Freedom House claim about January protesters over Wakashio remains unresolved.
open_questions: Did the crowd include at least 50 participants?
Was the crowd organized or a spontaneous audience at the hearing?
Did the police take any listed response action against this crowd?
Is this distinct from the unspecified Wakashio-related January protest described by Freedom House?

title: Avengers civic gathering on government handling of the Kistnen and Wakashio cases
organizer: The Avengers legal group; named lawyers and civic activists addressed the gathering
participants_original: The opened Defimedia report calls it a “grosse foule” (large crowd) without a number. An L’Express 2 February search excerpt says it gathered “une dizaine de milliers de personnes” (about ten thousand); a Mauritius Times interview excerpt quotes an attendee describing a very large crowd. The latter two pages were not opened.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending direct verification: the L’Express search-only excerpt gives an approximate ten-thousand attendance estimate, while opened Defimedia coverage independently describes a large crowd but no number. Because the numeric page was not opened and search-only evidence must remain pending_evidence, the threshold is not resolved in this dossier.

start_date.summary: The opened article identifies the gathering as Sunday 31 January 2021.

end_date.summary: The page describes speakers on stage from 09:30 to 14:00 and named leaders leaving around 14:07, but does not establish when the crowd physically dispersed. The physical end date remains unknown.

location.summary: The article places the gathering at the taxi stand in La Louise, Quatre-Bornes.

organizer.summary: The article identifies the Avengers legal group and quotes its lawyers/activists speaking.

demands.summary: Speakers criticized state handling of the Kistnen case, sought truth/justice, called for the DCP to leave, and challenged the prime minister over Wakashio. The category is political behavior/process.

participants_original.summary: Opened Defimedia describes a large crowd without number; L’Express search-only text reports “une dizaine de milliers” (~10,000); Mauritius Times search-only interview reports an attendee’s qualitative description of a very large crowd.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The search-only L’Express figure would exceed 50, but the page was not directly opened. Opened Defimedia’s qualitative “grosse foule” is supportive but not a numeric threshold by itself; leave pending evidence.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not report violence by people attending this gathering.

state_response.summary: The article says the PMO told the press it would consider the allegations; it does not show a formal government meeting, concession, arrest, beating, dispersal, killing, shooting or deliberate ignoring of the assembly. Response codes remain unknown.

notes: This was an Avengers-led civic/legal meeting, not a political-party election-support rally. Its public speeches explicitly addressed government and police conduct. A separate L’Express search excerpt reports about ten thousand attendees, but that page could not be opened; eligibility is now pending evidence rather than treating the snippet as verified. The opened Defi Media page currently shows a July 2026 publication date although the search index dates the story to early 2021; corroborate the original publication and attendance before resolving eligibility. The speaking program and leaders’ departure do not establish the physical end of the crowd; no end date is assigned. Do not merge with the separate 7 or 12 January court gatherings, the August 2020 Wakashio marches, or the February 2021 opposition march.
open_questions: Can the L’Express estimate of roughly ten thousand attendees be verified from the opened page or another contemporaneous source?
Can the attendance claim be checked in the page text or a further independent contemporaneous source?
Does any source give a participant number or clear threshold evidence?
Were any response actions taken by the state against the gathering?
Is the Wakashio-related demand a distinct issue or part of the same gathering?
When did the crowd physically disperse? The speakers’ program end and leaders’ departure do not establish this.

title: Court-side demonstration demanding Sawmynaden’s resignation
location: New Court House / Cathedral Square area, Port Louis
organizer: Unknown; LALIT attributes the crowd’s gathering to Bruneau Laurette, without independent corroboration.
participants_original: A 9 January L’Express search excerpt says “des centaines de manifestants” (hundreds of demonstrators) demanded Sawmynaden’s resignation on Thursday 7 January. An 8 January L’Express search excerpt also says Mauritians came to support Simla Kistnen outside court; it gives no number. ION News search text says bystanders gathered near the court but gives no number. The Le Xournal search excerpt also says many bystanders were near court, but gives no number. Neither the L’Express nor ION article page could be opened by this worker.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending direct verification: the L’Express search excerpt says hundreds, while the opened LALIT account and ION search excerpt describe a crowd. The L’Express and ION pages failed open and ordinary HTTPS recovery failed local DNS, so the specific threshold claim remains pending_evidence.

start_date.summary: The L’Express result describes Thursday 7 January; ION News is dated 7 January and refers to Sawmynaden’s court appearance; LALIT identifies his first appearance as 7 January. An 8 January L’Express result describes the previous day’s court gathering.

location.summary: The L’Express result locates demonstrators at New Court House; ION says bystanders gathered near court; LALIT places the crowd in Cathedral Square. An 8 January L’Express result describes people outside court and says the planned Cathedral Square location had to change under access restrictions.

organizer.summary: LALIT attributes assembling the Cathedral Square crowd to Bruneau Laurette. This is a single political-organization account and is not independently verified; organizer remains uncertain.

demands.summary: The L’Express search excerpt says demonstrators loudly demanded Minister Sawmynaden’s resignation. The article page could not be opened, so the code remains pending evidence.

participants_original.summary: L’Express search excerpt says “hundreds”; ION says bystanders gathered but gives no number; opened LALIT commentary calls it a crowd. An 8 January L’Express excerpt says people came to support Simla Kistnen, with no count. Le Xournal search text also calls the people near court “many bystanders” without a number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The excerpt’s “hundreds” would satisfy the threshold, and two other accounts describe a crowd, but the specific L’Express number is only search-only and direct page recovery failed; keep pending_evidence. The 8 January L’Express excerpt adds qualitative attendance but no number. Le Xournal also says many bystanders were present, but this qualitative search excerpt does not establish the threshold.

protester_violence.summary: LALIT alleges a disorderly subgroup from the gathered crowd attacked the minister’s car as it left. This is not independently corroborated; the coded value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: ION search excerpt mentions one person arrested that morning but does not establish that person was a participant or that the arrest was a response to the demonstration; other response dimensions are not resolved. All seven values remain unknown.

notes: Treat as distinct from the 12 January gathering unless evidence proves continuity. A 11 January invitation for minister supporters to attend on 12 January was a plan, not evidence of a separate protest; the separate minister-supporting group on 12 January should not be merged with this anti-minister crowd. LALIT’s organizer and car-attack claims remain attributed and uncorroborated.
open_questions: Can the L’Express report’s hundreds and resignation demand be verified from article text or another contemporary source?
Did the gathering end on 7 January, and what response if any was directed at it?
Can the ION News report’s arrest be tied to a demonstrator?
Was Bruneau Laurette an organizer or only present, and is that independently documented?
Is the car-attack allegation independently corroborated?
